text: Organised religion is basically a control mechanism dressed up as comfort. Strip away the rituals and you're left with a centuries-old protection racket trading guilt for obedience.
note: Criticises religion as an institution, no group dehumanised

text: Capitalism isn't broken, it's working exactly as designed: extract value, externalise the harm, repeat until the planet's a husk. Calling it a 'disease' is almost too kind.
note: Attacks an economic system, not people

text: Honestly this whole lecture reads like a corporate ad for late-stage capitalism. Where's the critique of who actually benefits?
note: Sharp critique of ideology and the course itself

text: The current government is sliding straight into fascism — purging the courts, muzzling the press, rewriting the rules so they can never lose. That's not democracy, that's a captured state.
note: Political critique of a government, no incitement

text: Communism looks beautiful on paper and turns into a meat grinder every single time it touches power. Every. Single. Time. The ideology has a body count problem it refuses to face.
note: Strong critique of an ideology, not a protected group

text: Oh sure, the prosperity gospel is *totally* spiritual — nothing says 'love thy neighbour' like a pastor with three private jets telling broke people their poverty is a faith deficiency. Inspiring stuff.
note: Sarcastic critique of a religious movement and a figure

text: I used to be devout and leaving the faith felt like waking up. The doctrine kept me terrified of an eternity of fire just for asking questions. That's not love, that's emotional captivity.
note: Personal critique of doctrine, own experience

text: The IMF's structural adjustment programmes gutted public health across the global south and called it reform. The institution should be on trial, not handing out advice.
note: Critique of an institution and its policy

text: Neoliberalism is the air we breathe and that's exactly the problem — it convinced everyone there's no alternative, so we stopped imagining one. Most poisonous idea of the last fifty years.
note: Ideological critique, metaphor not literal harm

text: The President is a vain, incompetent grifter who'd sell the constitution for a flattering headline. Worst leader this country has produced in living memory.
note: Harsh criticism of a single public figure

text: Nationalism is a hell of a drug. It takes ordinary people and convinces them a line on a map is worth dying and killing for. The whole ideology runs on manufactured grievance.
note: Critique of nationalism as an idea

text: Tech-utopianism is just eschatology for engineers. Same promise of salvation, same demand for faith, except the rapture is an AGI and the priests have stock options.
note: Witty critique of an ideology, no group targeted

text: The Church spent centuries covering for abusers and moving them parish to parish. As an institution it has forfeited any claim to moral authority. Burn the bureaucracy down (metaphorically) and start over.
note: Institutional critique, hyperbole flagged as metaphor

text: Astrology as a worldview annoys me — it dresses up cold reading as cosmic wisdom and tells people the stars excuse their choices. Fun party trick, terrible philosophy of life.
note: Dismissive critique of a belief system
